brief:
We Are Not Numbers reported that Palestinians in Gaza describe fear as a constant presence in their daily lives. Residents characterized the pervasive anxiety as a familiar companion rather than a temporary state, reflecting the sustained strain of living conditions in the territory.

The account highlights how security concerns have become normalized in Gaza's social fabric, shaping residents' experiences and psychological state as an ongoing reality rather than an exceptional circumstance.
dek: For Palestinians in Gaza fear has become a familiar companion.
title: Gaza residents describe fear as permanent condition amid ongoing crisis
